hook
Every time a car moves, thousands of tiny explosions are happening under the hood. Here's how a piston turns them into motion.
parts
Inside the engine is a cylinder. A piston slides up and down inside it, linked by a rod to a crankshaft.
parts
At the top are two valves, one to let air and fuel in, one to let exhaust out, and a spark plug.
intake
Stroke one: intake. The piston moves down, the intake valve opens, and a mix of air and fuel is sucked in.
compress
Stroke two: compression. Both valves close, and the piston squeezes the mixture into a tiny space.
power
Stroke three: power. The spark plug fires! The mixture explodes and slams the piston down with huge force.
exhaust
Stroke four: exhaust. The exhaust valve opens, and the piston pushes the burnt gas out.
cycle
Intake, compression, power, exhaust. Then it repeats, over and over.
crank
The crankshaft is the clever part. It turns the piston's up and down motion into spinning, just like your legs pedalling a bicycle.
multi
Real engines have four, six, or even eight pistons, firing one after another, so the power flows smoothly.
rpm
At highway speed, each piston completes this whole cycle about twenty five times every second!
outro
Tiny explosions, perfectly timed. That's what moves your car! Follow for more science made simple.
